plan: Store the workspace as a deep-copied dict tree (composite pattern): notes/references are leaves, sections/groups are containers with 'items' lists, so one shape serves all operations.

Implement each summary as a single recursive function dispatching on 'kind': total_word_count sums note word counts (markers stripped before \b\w+\b matching) and reference word_count fields; unresolved_markers unions note-text marker identifiers with reference 'unresolved' lists, then dedupes and sorts.
Render outline() by depth-first traversal in list order, emitting the workspace title then '  ' * level + '<kind>: <title>' with top-level items at level 1.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers, reject destinations inside the moved item's own subtree, and bounds-check the insertion index against the destination length — all before any mutation, so any ValueError leaves to_data() unchanged.
Perform the mutation as pop-from-parent then append/insert into destination, which preserves the item's subtree identically; to_data() returns a deep copy so callers cannot mutate internal state.
mechanisms: recursive composite tree of container and leaf items
uniform recursive dispatch on item kind for all summaries
recursive aggregation for total word count
deterministic depth-first outline traversal in list order
containment invariant: container-only destinations plus subtree no-cycle check
atomic move via full validation before any mutation
